findings.evidence: `∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f (max x 0)` for `t ≤ 0` is `-∫ x in t..0, f 0 = t * f 0`; no lemma in the file states this, and the body is not exposed.
findings.fix: Add `bernsteinPrimitive_of_nonpos {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≤ 0) : bernsteinPrimitive c f t = c + t * f 0` (needs `f` continuous on `Ici 0`), or an `EqOn`-based uniqueness lemma pinning the function on all of ℝ.
findings.issue: `bernsteinPrimitive` is public without `@[expose]` (unlike `IsCompletelyMonotone`, which is `@[expose] def` at CompletelyMonotone/Basic.lean:74), and the only value lemmas are `bernsteinPrimitive_zero` and `bernsteinPrimitive_eq` (`0 ≤ t`). Nothing characterizes `t < 0`, where the `max` extension makes the value `c + t * f 0`. A consumer therefore cannot prove any equation between `bernsteinPrimitive c f` and another function, so the definition is not extensionally determined by its API.

findings.evidence: grep for `IsBernsteinFunction` shows no `congr` lemma anywhere in the repo; `IsCompletelyMonotone.congr` and `IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.congr` (line 304) exist and are used by this very PR at Integral.lean:118.
findings.fix: Add `IsBernsteinFunction.congr (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) (h : Set.EqOn g f (Ici 0)) : IsBernsteinFunction g` to `Bernstein/Basic.lean` (all four clauses are within-`Ici 0`/`Ioi 0`, so it is provable, mirroring `IsCompletelyMonotone.congr` at CompletelyMonotone/Basic.lean:168), then restate `isBernsteinFunction_integral` about `fun t ↦ ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f x`.
findings.issue: `isBernsteinFunction_integral` is documented as "the primitive vanishing at the origin" and named for the integral, but its statement is just `IsBernsteinFunction (bernsteinPrimitive 0 f)` — a `le_rfl` instance of the previous theorem that adds no content and never mentions `∫ x in 0..t, f x`. The form a consumer actually meets, `IsBernsteinFunction (fun t ↦ ∫ x in (0:ℝ)..t, f x)`, is not derivable from the exposed API because `IsBernsteinFunction` has no congruence lemma.

findings.evidence: Bernstein/Basic.lean:86, 90, 94, 104 all use `@[grind →]`/`@[grind =>]`; Integral.lean:51 and 86 have none, and only `bernsteinPrimitive_zero` is `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Annotate `deriv_bernsteinPrimitive` with `@[grind =>]` (and `bernsteinPrimitive_eq` likewise) so `grind` can discharge derivative and value side goals about the primitive.
findings.issue: `deriv_bernsteinPrimitive` and `bernsteinPrimitive_eq` are the characteristic lemmas of the new definition but carry no automation annotation, while every accessor in `Bernstein/Basic.lean` (`contDiffOn`, `nonneg`, `deriv_nonneg`, `deriv_isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi`) carries `@[grind]`.

summary: The new `bernsteinPrimitive` is exposed as a public non-`@[expose]` definition whose value is pinned by lemmas only on `[0, ∞)`, so downstream cannot determine or rewrite the function it denotes off the half-line; and `isBernsteinFunction_integral` is named for the integral but is a `le_rfl` specialization that never states the integral form, which is unavailable because `IsBernsteinFunction` has no `congr`/EqOn lemma. Characteristic lemmas also carry no automation annotations, unlike every sibling in `Bernstein/Basic.lean`.
